conventions.convention: The charged comparison has finite quantum characteristic e≥2. For q_H≠1, residues are labels for q_H^i; for q_H=1, char F=e and the spectral values are i·1_F. The arbitrary-base auxiliary presentations also admit parameters outside this charged scope.
Cyclotomic relations are imposed on the first polynomial generator; induction appends strands on the right. Rank zero is F, including level zero; positive rank at level zero is the zero algebra.
The type-A parameters are Q(i,i+1)=v−u and Q(i+1,i)=u−v for e≥3, and Q(0,1)=Q(1,0)=−(u−v)^2 for e=2. The source crossing is ψ=−τ; its braid difference is ψ_rψ_(r+1)ψ_r−ψ_(r+1)ψ_rψ_(r+1).

Murphy and Schur cell modules use right actions. The Schur algebra is End_H(M) with ordinary composition. Types are exactly multipartitions, and a type-component-a label may occupy only physical components b≤a.
The Jantzen deformation is z=q_Ht and U_a=Q_at^(na), with the final rank n kept fixed at every auxiliary rank. J coefficients are integers and vanish unless λ strictly dominates μ.

For equal nonzero coefficients and nonzero exponent difference N, the valuation at t=1 is 1 in characteristic zero and p^(v_p(|N|)) in characteristic p. The zero Laurent difference has no finite valuation.
Equal hubs together with equal size are equivalent to equal residue content. Core switches preserve the hub; a switch with γ≥3 strictly decreases core size.

The transported grading is attached to fixed admissible normalizing series. Different choices are graded-isomorphic, but the underlying identity need not be graded; individual blocks can have trivial grading.

load_bearing.statement: On each charged central content sector, the named dots are commuting nilpotents; the displayed p/P series satisfy the stated scalar and intertwiner identities, and invertible q/Q normalizers exist, with the explicit source candidates satisfying the stated compatibility identities.

For the standard homogeneous cyclic affine type-A cyclotomic KLR quotient over any field, with finite e≥2 and level ℓ, B_d has dimension ℓ^d d! for d>0, and B_0=F has dimension one; level zero gives B_d=0 for d>0.
For R=Z[z±1,U_1±1,…,U_ℓ±1], ℓ≥1, the actual nondegenerate cyclotomic presentation has R-basis X^aT_w with 0≤a_r<ℓ and w∈S_n; this basis specializes to every commutative R-algebra.

Over the universal Laurent parameter ring, the standard multipartition Murphy elements form a dominance-cellular basis, their higher spans are two-sided ideals, and every commutative unit-parameter specialization inherits that basis and cell law.

The coefficient functional at the zero-dot identity-permutation PBW word is symmetric, and τ(ab) is a perfect associative R-bilinear pairing; both properties survive every commutative unit-parameter base change.

Evaluation identifies Hom_H(M_ν,M_μ) with M_μ∩Hm_ν, with rectangular semistandard sums as its R-basis. The corresponding actual endomorphisms form a free dominance-cellular basis of End_H(M), specializing to every commutative unit-parameter base.

In the stated universal generic and Lyle–Mathas deformation fields, det G_(λν) is the product over semistandard T of γ_(t_T)/(C_(t_T)u_T); the monic transition determinant is exactly 1, and an empty weight determinant is 1.

For any field, charged nondegenerate parameter of finite order e≥2, and the specified rank-n deformation, every actual multipartition Schur weight satisfies V(det G_(λν))=Σ_μ J_(λμ)K_(μν), with finite valuations of every retained foot difference.

Under the stated arbitrary-field, arbitrary-level charged nondegenerate hypotheses, the actual Schur Jantzen filtration is radical-first and terminating, and Σ_(s>0)[Δ_F(λ)^s]=Σ_μ J_(λμ)[Δ_F(μ)] in the integer Grothendieck group.

For finite e≥2, ℓ≥1 and integer charges, nonminimum componentwise cores admit same-hub switch paths that never increase size and end at strictly smaller size; minimum cores of the same hub and charges are connected by equal-size switches.

Over the original field in both finite-quantum-characteristic branches, every central content idempotent is zero or primitive, and its nonzero terms are exactly all primitive central idempotents; rank zero and positive-rank level zero have the stated boundary conventions.

concerns.concern: The title claims 'content-preserving descent', whereas the Statement and proof preserve the hub and allow strict size decrease. This cannot preserve core residue content. Explicitly, for e=2, ℓ=2 and charges (0,0), the componentwise cores ((1),(2,1)) have height matrix [[0,-2],[-2,0]] and content (2,2). The permitted γ=4 switch produces [[-1,-1],[-1,-1]], representing two empty cores with content (0,0). The same overstatement appears in F2 of thm-cyclotomic-multipartitions-of-fixed-content-are-jantzen-connected: 'content-preserving descent' and 'within a content class ... cores'. Its later fixed-rank lift construction supplies content preservation for lifts, not for the descending cores. The lemma's actual same-hub Statement is not refuted by this example; the title and downstream attributed fact need correction.

The Review status paragraph says the comparison 'still requires the complete normalizing-series and colour-pattern calculations' and that trace perfectness, center lifting and the off-support signed rim-hook calculation remain open. Current items now contain explicit arguments for these: normalization Steps 2.1–6.1, canonical-trace Steps 2.2–5.1, degenerate-center Steps 2.1–6.1, and rim-hook-valuation Steps 9.1–11.1. Reconcile this page description with the current carriers and any genuinely unresolved supplier obligations; presence of these proofs alone does not certify them.

The Statement identifies multipartition K_(μν) as 'the semistandard Kostka number of' def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number. That published Definition covers ordinary partitions and positive-integer labels. The actual multipartition types, component flag and K_(λ,ν) are defined in def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules. Cite that exact defining interface rather than attributing the larger domain to the ordinary definition.

seams_checked.note: The ordinary cellular and JM suppliers are used for their stated interfaces. The fixed-core argument explicitly carries the signed-conjugate Murphy/Dipper–James dictionary rather than identifying the two conventions without transport.
The cyclic Cartan datum, finite e≥2 and e=2 double edge are preserved. The regular-Hom calculation uses vanishing Cartan column sums and keeps the grading variable independent of q_H.

The specialization preserves the native dot-move convention and explicitly sets ψ=−τ with the corresponding braid order. The normalizer conventions also match [Brundan–Kleshchev §§3.3–4.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0808.2032).

The standard homogeneous quotient, first-strand relation, right-append functors and basic adjunction are preserved. The dimension argument specializes categorical shifts at v=1 and does not import conditional global-basis conclusions.

Core independence and the size/weight formula retain their finite-e hypotheses. The level-one block theorem is transferred to Murphy modules through the explicitly stated conjugation and common sign pullback.

The consumer counterexample's F3 uses the arbitrary-base affine presentation and level-one relation X_1=Q faithfully. Its characteristic-zero degenerate example uses the auxiliary presentation, not the finite-e charged degenerate specialization. The page currently lists its parent as its direct prerequisite.

The finite cyclic consumers preserve the type-A signs, module-side conversion and chosen-series grading. Infinite-order and integer-color local dictionaries explicitly use the arbitrary-base auxiliary presentations and supply their own comparisons; they do not instantiate the finite-e bridge outside its scope.
